name: HabiBench
subtitle: An Open Multimodal Benchmark for Reliable UK Terrestrial Habitat Assessment
blurb: HabiBench is developing an open benchmark for reliable habitat assessment by combining ground-level photographs, Earth-observation embeddings and ecological text from open, expert-audited data. It evaluates classification accuracy alongside calibrated uncertainty, the contribution of each modality and robustness when evidence is missing—helping establish when automated assessment can support or triage a field visit.
role: Lead applicant and Principal Investigator; leads the technical programme at the University of Lincoln.
funding: £22,278 awarded through the EPSRC-funded UK Open Multimodal AI Network, OMAIB Round 2.
outputs: reliability-aware evaluation protocol and OMAIB leaderboard
partners: James Brown and Lan Qie — co-investigators, University of Lincoln

name: AI-Hab
subtitle: Ground-level computer vision for UK habitat assessment
blurb: Automated habitat assessment from UKCEH Countryside Survey photographs. Over 5,000 expert-labelled images across 18 UKHab-aligned classes; nine convolutional and vision-transformer architectures compared under one reproducible pipeline. The resulting paper, code and demonstrator provide the empirical foundation for the broader HabiBench programme.
role: Lead for AI model development and quantitative analysis. NERC-funded University of Lincoln–UKCEH collaboration.
why: Upload a photograph of a field and the model tells you what habitat it is. The fastest way to see whether the research actually works.

name: FedFSC
subtitle: Few-shot client updates for heterogeneous federated learning
blurb: Reference implementation of few-shot client updates for heterogeneous federated learning, accompanying the DistributedML 2023 paper.

name: Pezego
subtitle: AI-assisted pest-management decision support
blurb: A mobile pest-management tool for agronomists and farmers. Contributed LLM-based multi-agent methods for generating informed, situation-specific treatment recommendations.
role: Research Assistant, University of Sheffield. Algorithm development and lead author on the resulting preprint.
